title: Referral and word-of-mouth with measured loop maths
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether a referral or word-of-mouth play is worth running and how to read its effect without overstating incrementality.
applies_when: Customer base at or above the referral minimum
required_inputs: Invites per customer and invite conversion (measured)
evidence_requirements: Invites sent per user over a window
Time from signup to the invitee's signup
'How did you hear about us' counts
Recent product, service, price or staff changes
missing_data_behavior: No measured invite rates: no viral claims; K never defaulted.
Small base: owner asks personally; no programme maths.

decision_branches.then: Seeded total = seed / (1 - K); a multiplier on other channels, not growth on its own.
Treat as unproven; re-measure; never forecast unbounded growth.
Keep review work (local reviews matter even though the book downplays negative word of mouth).

implementation_steps: Measure invites per user and conversion (split into click-through and signup)
Count WOM and referral sources per 100 customers
Check whether the customer base is large enough
Design one share moment and a story worth retelling
dependencies: Activation works; referrals feed a leak otherwise (PB-referrals avoidWhen)
Enough experienced customers for WOM to exist (PB-referrals requires 20)

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: Engineering for in-product loops (the book cites months of work)

metrics: K = invites per user × invite conversion
guardrails: Referred customers aren't all incremental; label the outcome.
No copied invite text or bought lists.
No 'exponential' or 'viral' claims unless measured K ≥ 1
Consent for any invite emails; no address-book spam
No fake or undisclosed incentivised reviews or endorsements
Don't treat NPS as WOM volume
Don't credit all referred customers as incremental
alternatives_when_constrained: No event tracking: referral codes per customer
Too few customers: borrow others' credibility (partners, creators) or build reach first
stop_conditions: PB-referrals stop rule (under 3% of customers share after 4 weeks)
Review negative-WOM handling only after a real change
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Incentivised referrals can attract low-quality users or breach platform rules
Public reviews differ from conversational WOM: they persist and are read by in-market searchers, so the book's 'negative WOM rarely matters' doesn't carry over to a low local rating
Disruptive new categories where people must see the product in use (the book notes WOM matters more there)

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: add viralCoefficient(invitesPerUser, inviteConversion) and seededTotal(seed, K) for K<1 to shared/growth/calc.ts; plays cite these numbers instead of writing them.
proposed: no viral-growth claim without measured K ≥ 1 over a stated window.
proposed: A plan for a business with under about 20 customers can't make referrals or WOM the bankable play (aligns with PB-referrals customers_min).
proposed: Referral and WOM forecasts scale with the customer base and are labelled partly non-incremental.
proposed: A single negative post or review triggers a fix-and-respond action, not a strategy change, unless it reflects a real product, service or staff change.
proposed: NPS is not used as a measure of WOM volume.

external_requirement.rule: proposed: Review and referral incentives follow platform rules and consumer-protection disclosure law.

reconciliation_note: Adds loop arithmetic and incrementality labels to PB-referrals (backlog CG-19, CG-39).
